Fed governor Lisa Cook: "No legitimate basis for removal" on Trump mortgage claims
market.summary: Lawyers for Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook have submitted their case for why she cannot legally be fired, as President Trump seeks new avenues for dismissing the Biden appointee for cause. The big picture: After the Supreme Court ruled against Trump's attempt to fire Cook last year over allegations that she claimed two different properties as her primary residence in mortgage documents, the White House has sought to introduce a more formal process in pursuit of the same goal. It is a closely watched case that may determine the political independence of America's central bank, by setting how high the bar is for a president to fire Fed governors. Driving the news: Three weeks ago, the White House asked for her response to the substance of those allegations, which her lawyers submitted — and distributed to reporters — Wednesday evening. Cook's lawyers argue that "there is no legitimate basis for" removing Cook from the Fed board, where her term extends to 2034, and that the purported errors were "an entirely inadvertent oversight." They say that she was fully transparent with her lender and note media reports that Trump himself and five members of his cabinet have also had dubious claims of primary residency on a property in the past. Catch up quick: Trump announced that he was firing Cook about a year ago for cause, alleging mortgage fraud after housing finance regulator Bill Pulte showed she had mortgage applications for two separate properties as a primary residence in a short time frame. The Federal Reserve Act gives governors of the central bank 14-year terms to insulate them from politics, but says the president can remove them "for cause." The Supreme Court ruled that Cook could stay in her job while the attempted firing is adjudicated, but did not lay out precise criteria of what clears the bar of firing a Fed governor for cause or how a president must establish it. In an apparent effort to establish legal cause, White House deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino wrote to Cook earlier this month citing the apparent mortgage application errors and asking for her defense. What they're saying: "The process for seeking financing for the Atlanta condominium… began with Governor Cook using the lender's website to seek information about a 'vacation home' mortgage — a clear indication of the loan type she was looking to acquire," wrote Abbe David Lowell, Cook's attorney. "The lender, which previously worked with Governor Cook to refinance her Massachusetts property earlier that year, knew that she had lived in Michigan for more than 15 years and worked full-time as a tenured professor at Michigan State University. Governor Cook gave no indication that she was leaving to take any new job in Atlanta," Lowell wrote. Other documents how that Cook "regularly indicated her 'primary residence' or 'permanent residence' to be Michigan" and she "confirmed that her Atlanta property was a '2nd Home.'" "Governor Cook's actions demonstrate that there was no intentional misconduct and zero intent to defraud or mislead." Of note: Lowell cites media reports of Trump himself and several cabinet members making dubious claims of a property's primary residence status, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The other side: The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. What's next: The question now is whether Trump again attempts to fire Cook, with more of a review process — and if so, how the courts respond.

HUBG.summary: A shareholder class action lawsuit has been filed against Hub Group, Inc. alleging false and misleading statements regarding premature transaction recognition, understatement of costs, and ineffective internal controls. HUBG.title: Hub Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: HUBG) Faces New Scrutiny: Nasdaq Non-Compliance Notice Over Late Form 10-Q Amid Securities Class Action- Hagens Berman
HUBG.summary: Hub Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: HUBG) has received a Nasdaq non-compliance notice for failing to timely file its Form 10-Q quarterly report. OTCM.title: PesoRama Inc. Begins Trading on OTCQX Best Market
OTCM.summary: PesoRama Inc., a Canadian dollar store operator in Mexico under the JOi Dollar Plus brand, has upgraded from the Pink Limited Market to trade on OTCQX Best Market under ticker PSSOF. LGND.title: Ligand to Participate in September Investor Conferences

Wainwright 28th Annual Global Investment Conference (September 14). The company will host fireside chats and one-on-one meetings with investors at these events.

UNH.title: The AI Honeymoon is Over: Momentum AI Austin 2026 Unveils Full C-Suite Agenda and Premier Sponsors to Drive Enterprise ROI
UNH.summary: Reuters Events announced Momentum AI Austin 2026, an enterprise AI summit scheduled for September 24-25, 2026, bringing together over 500 senior leaders including CIOs, CTOs, and Chief AI Officers. EUDA.summary: EUDA Health Holdings Limited announced that its subsidiary Melana International Pte. Ltd. was recognized as a winner of the SME100 Awards 2026 Singapore. SGLY.title: Singularity and AKD Development Inc. Enter Into Development Services Framework Agreement for Florence, South Carolina Data Center and Power Infrastructure Project
SGLY.summary: Singularity Future Technology Ltd (NASDAQ: SGLY) has entered into a Master Development Services Framework Agreement with AKD Development Inc. for potential development of a data center and power infrastructure in Florence, South Carolina. KCDMY.summary: Bunzl Canada donated 68,000 rolls of toilet paper to Food Banks Canada on National Toilet Paper Day, marking its largest donation to date. DCO.title: Ducommun to Participate in Jefferies Industrials Conference
DCO.summary: Ducommun Incorporated announced that CEO Stephen G. Oswald will participate in the Jefferies Industrials Conference on September 9, 2026, with a general presentation at 11:30 a.m. Eastern and one-on-one investor meetings scheduled throughout the day. ZH.title: Zhihu Inc. Reports Unaudited Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
ZH.summary: Zhihu Inc. reported Q2 2026 revenues of RMB690.1 million, down 3.7% year-over-year, with a net loss of RMB37.4 million compared to net income of RMB72.5 million in Q2 2025. Gross margin declined to 57.0% from 62.5%, primarily due to increased content-related costs. However, the company showed some positive signs with paid content and IP operations revenue growing year-over-year, and adjusted operating losses narrowing by 32.0%. The company maintained disciplined cost management with total operating expenses down 13.0% and continued share repurchases.

PYPTF.title: PayPoint plc : Director/PDMR Shareholding

SYANY.title: AL Sydbank fastholder momentum i andet kvartal

VSH.summary: Vishay Intertechnology announced four new AEC-Q200 qualified automotive-grade common mode chokes (ICM5050-A, ICM6050-A, IFLN-1210BE-A, IFLN-1812CZ-A) that offer low DCR (0.4-12 mΩ), high current capability up to 14 A, and impedance up to 11 kΩ at 100 MHz. AVEX.title: AEVEX Corp. Notice of October 20, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline
